newsitem.title: UK: Dollar holds gains vs battered yen in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar holds gains vs battered yen in late Europe.

text.p: The dollar was holding on to the bulk of the day's gains against the yen by late European trade, steady but just shy of the three-and-a-half-year highs seen in earlier trade today.
Analysts cited yield differentials, an uncertain political backdrop in Japan and technical factors as reasons to sell off the yen, which also saw it suffer against the mark and sterling.

"Dollar/yen has nearly hit our target for the year/end but it may not be over yet," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull. "We probably won't see the end (of yen weakness) until Japan puts rates up."
The dollar rose to 114.40 yen in earlier trade, a level not seen April 1993. By 1559 GMT, the dollar was trading at 114.21/31 yen against 113.22/27 late Friday in Europe.
Analysts said the hung parliament that resulted from Japan's general election on October 20 has created some political uncertainty with the coalition partners yet to form a new government.
"The political situation is uneasy at the moment and while that's going on there's no chance of the Bank of Japan moving up rates," said David Bloom, U.S. economist at HSBC James Capel in London.
Analysts see Japanese economic growth faltering and a further deterioriation of its trade account while fiscal and monetary policy bias is expected to be easier, all adding up to a weaker yen.
Chartists said the next upside targets for dollar/yen are previous support levels at 115.00 and 115.85 which briefly held during the dollar's decline in the first half of 1993.

The mark was also stronger against the yen, ticking up to a 44-month high of 75.19 in earlier trade. At 1623 GMT, it was trading at 75.10/12 yen compared with 74.55/58 in late European trade on Friday.

The dollar against the mark was sidelined today, weighed by the mark's strength against the yen. It was also softened by dampened prospects of a German interest rate easing near-term, particularly after comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Friday saying he saw no need for cuts in the foreseeable future.
At 1640 GMT, the dollar was trading at its session lows of 1.5172/82 marks compared with 1.5190/95 late Friday.
Buoyant sterling retreated from key chart resistance at the 2.4560/80 marks while cable found support at $1.61 after touching a 16-month high at $1.6145.
By late trade, the pound was steady against the dollar but still within the day's ranges and sterling/mark had slipped below 2.45 marks.

The Canadian dollar was little changed from late Friday levels in Europe after the Bank of Canada made a 25 basis point cut in its bank rate to 3.50 percent. The Canadian dollar stood at C$1.3445/50 at 1658 GMT from C$1.3440/45 late Friday.
The South African rand recovered from an earlier all-time low of 4.67 per dollar amid concerns over the country's economic problems. It stood at 4.6630/80 in late Europe.
